GET STARTED

Bring your first
piece of work.

Amplifier Unified is an early adopter experience. You run the app on a host you control and connect the AI services you want to use.

Early adopter setup

A little preparation.
A useful first task.

Today’s setup involves installing the app, configuring AI access, and keeping the host available while you work.

The appOpen source · MIT licensed
Your AI accessConfigured separately
Your workspaceServed from your host
Questions before you begin?
01

Prepare a place to run it.

You’ll need Python and uv, plus a supported environment. Choose your platform to see the starting point.

Your platform
On a Mac

Use the macOS prerequisites and installation steps in the current setup guide. You’ll run Unified on your Mac and open its workspace in your browser.

Open the current setup guide
02

Connect your AI access.

Configure a supported provider using the app’s setup guidance. Your provider account, subscription, or API usage determines access and costs. Optional voice, images, and tools may need additional services.

Read the configuration documentation
03

Start with something small and real.

Open the workspace and bring a task you already understand. That makes it easier to inspect the result and decide what to change.

Choose a prompt to copy for your first conversation.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Know where the work
and the costs live.

The app’s license is separate from the terms and charges of your AI services. A locally running app may still send relevant data to the providers and tools you configure.

Keep the host running for ongoing work. Review access requests and tool behavior before using sensitive material.
